title_en: Sorry to Trouble You in Chinese

t: to go on a business trip
sentences.en: Next week I'm going on a business trip, and there'll be no one at home to water the flowers.
I went downstairs to find my neighbor Xiao Zhang and said: "Xiao Zhang, sorry to trouble you, could you water the flowers for me?"
Xiao Zhang said: "No problem, just give me the key."
I said: "Thank you, sorry for the trouble."
A week later, I came back, and discovered the flowers on the balcony had bloomed beautifully.
I bought Xiao Zhang some fruit, and said once more: "Sorry for the trouble."

t: to go on a business trip
sentences.en: Xiao Zhang held the fruit and said: "Next time you go on a trip, just call on me."

vocab: to go on a business trip

quiz.q: Why does the narrator ask Xiao Zhang for help?
a: To water the flowers during a business trip

quiz.q: What does 麻烦你了 express?
a: Thanks for the trouble someone took to help

quiz.q: What does the narrator discover after returning from the trip?
a: The flowers on the balcony have bloomed well

grammar.p: 麻烦你 + verb（asking a favor politely）
grammar.e: 麻烦你 before a verb softens a request — it shows you know the favor takes the other person's time or effort.
grammar.x: 麻烦你帮我浇水。— Sorry to trouble you, could you water them for me.

grammar.p: 麻烦你了（thanking someone for their trouble）
grammar.e: 麻烦你了 is said after someone has already helped — it thanks them for the specific effort or inconvenience, heavier than a plain 谢谢.
grammar.x: 谢谢你，麻烦你了。— Thank you, sorry for the trouble.

grammar.p: 把 + object + 给 + person（handing something over）
grammar.e: 把 moves the object in front of the verb to focus on what is being handed to someone.
grammar.x: 你把钥匙给我吧。— Just give me the key.
